- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥1.0) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast peak values by 2–5%.
- When sentiment is consistently negative (≤-1.0), model underestimates; increase forecast by 2–5% to align with downward momentum.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > true outcome by >10%), model often overcorrects; reduce subsequent forecast by 3–8% to avoid overshoot.
- If sentiment flips from negative to positive mid-period, model fails to adjust; check for lagged mean reversion — forecast should gradually rise toward historical mean.
- For 30-day horizon, model often overestimates early in the period (first 5–7 days) when sentiment is volatile; cap early forecast peaks at 10% below true mean of prior 10-day window.
- If sentiment history shows repeated “+1, -1, +1” cycles, model tends to misread momentum; apply smoothing filter to reduce oscillation in forecast slope.
